authoritativeAccess.name: Rockhouse public access
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Rockhouse Access
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: AGFC and The Nature Conservancy establish the named site's public identity and ownership. Natural Atlas independently maps Rockhouse Boat Launch at 36.28193372205891, -93.6639968409015 and classifies it as a gravel launch on Rockhouse Creek and the Kings River. At that exact point, current Esri World Imagery visibly shows the gravel access road and turnaround terminating at the west bank; a candidate-specific National Map query places it about 107 feet from the Kings River NHD centerline. The older local route-guide coordinate is rejected because it lands about 0.8 mile south in forest. This evidence class is retained for expert-reviewed corrections but is not whitelisted for unattended auto-apply.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Water edge where the mapped Rockhouse gravel launch road meets the west bank of the Kings River

authoritativeFacilityAnchor.name: Rockhouse public access
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.officialName: Rockhouse Access
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.extractionMethod: AGFC states that its McIlroy Madison County WMA property joins the Kings River at Rockhouse Access, and The Nature Conservancy independently identifies Rockhouse as the AGFC-owned public access just upstream from the preserve. Kings River Arkansas describes a gravel road, ample parking, and a large gravel-bar launch near Rockhouse Creek. The facility anchor is the center of the unmistakable gravel turnaround connected to the independently mapped Rockhouse Boat Launch in current Esri World Imagery; it is stored separately from the shoreline water entry. This evidence class records official access identity plus transparent aerial derivation and is intentionally excluded from the unattended auto-apply source whitelist.
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.coordinateText: Center of the gravel vehicle turnaround immediately west of the Rockhouse shoreline landing in current Esri World Imagery

authoritativeAccess.name: Tyler Bend River Access Point Upper
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Tyler Bend river access
aliases: Tyler Bend River Access Point Upper
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The official NPS Tyler Bend area map marks the boat launch on the upstream/west side of the bend. The 2026 NPS concession operating plan removes the competing downstream feature from consideration by stating that only the Upper Tyler Bend access is available. The selected coordinate is the mapped upper gravel slipway, whose access road and shoreline landing align with current Esri World Imagery and the official map; the similarly named lower OSM slipway is not the currently authorized launch.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Water edge of the Upper Tyler Bend gravel slipway selected by the official NPS area map and current operating plan

authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The current Delaware tidal-access guide identifies Seaford as a four-lane Nanticoke River public access area and Woodland Wharf as an unimproved/carry-top Nanticoke access. DNREC documents Woodland Wharf’s public canoe/kayak dock, parking, bulkhead, and Fish & Wildlife management. Coordinates are public facility and near-water anchors; verify current carry, exact wetted edge, ferry cable/vessel path, strong current, hours, parking, landing, and closure status before committing.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: DNREC-established public canoe/kayak dock and bulkhead near Woodland Ferry; stored point is an official water-quality/west-bank near-water anchor. Verify exact dock/wetted edge, strong current, ferry cable and vessel path, carry, parking, hours, landing, and closures before taking out.

authoritativeAccess.name: Lekwa Access #242
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Lekwa Access
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Story County identifies Lekwa Access #242 at 56156 130th Street as a managed South Skunk River Water Trail access, and the official MyCountyParks record independently documents canoeing and kayaking with photographs of the signed access and its ramp reaching the river. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory feature (GlobalID a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c) describes a concrete launch with six parking stalls and a 33-foot parking-to-access distance. Current Esri World Imagery places that inventory coordinate at the visible water-side ramp edge immediately south of the 130th Street bridge. It is retained as the water entry; the NHD and route-projected alternatives 23 and 50 feet farther east are rejected because they move into the channel.

authoritativeAccess.name: Aqua Lane access
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Aqua Lane / Rice Lake carry-in
aliases: Rice Lake Carry-in Public Water Access Site
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The current Anoka County/RCWD Rice Creek Water Trail map places the Aqua Lane access immediately upstream of the road crossing, with limited parking east of the channel. Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02907 independently identifies the same Anoka County carry-in, specifies one gravel carry-in ramp and five-car parking, and records the access on the downstream-left bank at river mile 16.2. Because its heads-up-digitized GIS point falls at the bridge/facility rather than a shoreline edge, the water entry below is derived separately at the east-bank water edge visible immediately upstream of the bridge in current Esri World Imagery. The DNR feature remains the distinct authoritative facility anchor.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: East-bank shoreline immediately upstream of the Aqua Lane bridge, selected from the official access pin, DNR downstream-left bank attribute, and current aerial imagery

aliases: Rice Lake Carry-in Public Water Access Site

It documents one gravel carry-in ramp, one five-car parking lot, and the downstream-left bank. The heads-up-digitized GIS point is retained as the official facility/access anchor; the adjacent shoreline water entry is recorded separately by provider anoka_rice_creek_aqua_lane_water_entry.

authoritativeAccess.name: Lincoln Park Boat Ramp
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Lincoln Drive Park Landing
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Red River State Water Trail Map 4 identifies Lincoln Drive Park Landing on the left/Grand Forks bank at river mile 304.1 as the trailer-access put-in for the official two-mile trip to LaFave Park. Visit Grand Forks independently directs users to the Lincoln Park boat ramp from Belmont Road and 13th Avenue South. The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department inventory identifies the matching active Grand Forks Park District poured-concrete ramp as ObjectID 1427 at 47.90888410499237, -97.02268528004571. Current Esri World Imagery shows that official point on the upper ramp; the coordinate below is the adjacent water-side end of the same visible concrete ramp, about 79 feet away. The distinct official facility anchor is preserved by provider ndgf_lincoln_drive_park_ramp_access_anchor.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Map-derived water-side end of NDGF Fishing Facilities ObjectID 1427 concrete ramp; approximately 79 feet from the official facility anchor

authoritativeFacilityAnchor.name: Lincoln Park
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.officialName: Lincoln Drive Park Landing

Its published GIS point lies on the upper portion of the visible ramp and is retained as the official facility anchor, not substituted for the water-entry coordinate.
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.coordinateText: NDGF Fishing Facilities ObjectID 1427; active Grand Forks Park District poured-concrete ramp facility anchor

authoritativeAccess.officialName: Long Lake Boat Landing / Long Lake Regional Park
aliases: Long Lake Public Water Access Site
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS01204 identifies the GPS-collected south-shore Long Lake facility, administered by Ramsey County, with two concrete-slab ramps, one dock, and trailer parking. Its official coordinate lands directly on the visible concrete slipway and is about 15 feet from the independently mapped OSM slipway. The Anoka County/RCWD water-trail map identifies this exact Long Lake Boat Landing as the 15.2-mile full-route finish, distinct from the limited canoe access at Long Lake Beach farther north. The DNR GPS coordinate is therefore retained as the water entry rather than projected to the distant Rice Creek centerline.

entries.name: Rum River Central Regional Park north boat launch

authoritativeAccess.name: Rum River Central Regional Park access
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Rum River Central Regional Park north boat launch
aliases: Rum River Central Regional Park access
Rum River, Central Park N Public Water Access Site
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Rum River Map 3 places the Central Regional Park trailer access, watercraft campsites, toilets, and drinking water at river mile 13.8. This uniquely selects the north facility: Minnesota public-water-access record WAS02199 is explicitly Central Park N at river mile 13.8, while the distinct Central Park S record WAS00323 is at river mile 10.7 near the map's fishing-pier/rest-area context. Anoka County's park page and summer map independently identify both a boat launch and canoe/kayak launch. The water-entry coordinate is the mapped slipway 8 feet from WAS02199; current Esri World Imagery aligns it with the north launch at the river edge.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Water-side slipway at the Minnesota DNR WAS02199 Central Park N access; 8 feet from the official inventory anchor

Rum River, Central Park N Public Water Access Site
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02199 identifies Central Park N at river mile 13.8, administered by Anoka County, with a launch and one parking lot. The published GIS point is retained as the official facility/access anchor. The adjacent water-side slipway is represented separately by provider mn_dnr_rum_central_north_ramp_water_entry.

Decker Creek canoe and kayak access
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Nebraska Game and Parks identifies the canoe/kayak stop a few yards from the mouth of Decker Creek and publishes a photograph of the graded landing. Its Platte River Water Trail article gives the route topology: paddlers turn from the Platte up Decker Creek, pass under the railroad bridge, and reach the stop; the site was built as a river-accessible stop rather than a normal vehicle put-in/take-out, though boats may be wheeled down a maintenance road. The official photograph matches the uniquely shaped gravel landing, riprap, curved paved path, and footbridge visible in current Esri World Imagery. The coordinate is the water edge of that landing on the west bank of Decker Creek, immediately south of the footbridge.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Water edge of the photographed graded landing on the west bank of Decker Creek, immediately south of the footbridge

authoritativeAccess.name: Plum Creek Landing
authoritativeAccess.officialName: Plum Creek Landing
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The Wisconsin DNR public-access inventory identifies feature 835 as Plum Creek Landing, a state-owned carry-in on the Kickapoo River, and Crawford County independently lists the Plum Creek/Kickapoo Wild Woods Canoe Landing. Wisconsin River Trips documents the exact Plum Creek-to-Highway-60 trip, while Miles Paddled's Plum-Creek-to-Wauzeka report publishes 43.11429, -90.91274 for this put-in and 43.08471, -90.87906 for the distinct Wauzeka take-out. Current Esri World Imagery places the DNR coordinate at the water-side edge of the visible gravel turnaround. Candidate-centered NHD evidence independently places it inside the river polygon and 18 feet from the Kickapoo flowline, so the exact DNR coordinate is retained as the water entry.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Wisconsin DNR feature 835; visually confirmed at the gravel carry-in water edge
